summary: Structurally valid SDRF (parse_sdrf ms-proteomics + vertebrates exit 0, sdrf-tools check exit 0, all 13 controlled terms resolve live in OLS) with a correct 8-file mapping. It fails on one important design finding: the two SCX series (2013-03-22 and 2013-04-06) are encoded as technical replicates 1 and 2 of a single source / biological replicate 1. No accessible source documents that relationship, and the accessible evidence points to two separately prepared enrichment/SCX series rather than repeated measurements of the same samples. The primary source that would settle it (Weinert et al. 2013 Cell Rep full text, gold OA) was not consulted. Remaining findings are minor.

design_consistency.evidence: Recomputed: 8 runs = 2 series x 4 SCX fractions, label-free, single MaxQuant experiment (peptides.txt has only one aggregate 'Intensity' column, no per-experiment columns; summary.txt has no Experiment column). The SDRF encodes one source name, biological replicate 1, technical replicate 1 (0322 series) and 2 (0406 series). No source documents whether the second series is a re-injection, a separate enrichment of the same lysate, or a different animal. See important finding on the replicate structure.

omission_safety.evidence: Pass performed. Most values are traced to a source or are 'not available'. However, the single source name plus technical replicate 2 asserts that the 2013-04-06 series is a repeated measurement of the same sample as the 2013-03-22 series. That is more specific than any accessible evidence supports (the manifest itself labels it an inference). Omitted material evidence: the anti-succinyllysine antibody enrichment (optional characteristics[enrichment process]) and the differing autosampler volumes between series (manifest says 'identical LC-MS method' only).

findings.location: source name, characteristics[biological replicate], comment[technical replicate] rows 1-8 (rows 1-4 = 20130322 SCX_01..04 TR1; rows 5-8 = 20130406 scx_1..4 TR2)
findings.message: The two SCX series are asserted to be technical replicates (repeated measurements) of a single biological sample, but no evidence establishes that relationship. Accessible evidence suggests separately prepared series, and whether they come from the same liver lysate or from different animals (biological replicates) is unknown.
findings.evidence: Spec README: 'comment[technical replicate]: Repeated measurements of the same sample (e.g., multiple injections)'; 'characteristics[biological replicate]: Independent biological samples'. PRIDE sample protocol: enriched peptides 'were eluted ... and immediately seperated by micro-scale SCX chromatography', so each SCX series most plausibly follows its own enrichment. The series were acquired 15 days apart with a different naming scheme (SCX_0n vs scx_n) and different autosampler volumes (RAW headers: sample pickup 5.00 / loading 9.00 ul for 0322 vs 6.00 / 12.00 ul for 0406), with the same method 1-9um_BTW_141min_120MS2_IW2.meth. No sample names in headers. List_of_RAW_files.xlsx Notes are empty for all 8 files. MaxQuant pooled all 8 into one experiment (single Intensity column). PRIDE, the abstract and MeSH say nothing about the number of mice or enrichments. The manifest labels the encoding an inference.
findings.correction: Settle the relationship from the primary source: Weinert et al. 2013 Cell Rep 4:842-851, doi:10.1016/j.celrep.2013.07.024 (gold OA, CC BY-NC-ND; Experimental Procedures and Table S5 legend), retrieved via a browser or library copy, or by contacting the submitters. Re-injection of the same fractions or re-enrichment of the same lysate: the current encoding may stay, citing the source. Different animals: give the series distinct source names with biological replicate 1 and 2 and technical replicate 1. If the full text is consulted and is silent, keep the current encoding only with that negative result recorded in the manifest. Optionally add comment[sample preparation batch] to mark the two preparations.

findings.message: Trypsin/P comes from the MaxQuant search settings, not from a stated digestion protocol. The spec defines this column as the enzyme used for protein digestion. The PRIDE wording 'strict trypsin specificity' does not contradict Trypsin/P ('strict' = specific rather than semi-specific search), and it does not name a digest reagent.
findings.evidence: summary.txt Protease 'Trypsin/P', Max. missed cleavages 2; PRIDE data protocol '...with strict trypsin specificity, and allowing up to 2 missed cleavage sites'; sample protocol says only 'Peptides were prepared from the indicated samples'. Spec: 'Enzyme or chemical used for protein digestion', examples NT=Trypsin;AC=MS:1001251. sdrf-tools reconcile BLOCKER cleavage_agent_unsupported (would fire for any enzyme because the record has no digest sentence).
findings.correction: Prefer NT=Trypsin;AC=MS:1001251 for the digest reagent (trypsin is implied by 'trypsin specificity'). Keep Trypsin/P as the search rule in the manifest. Or keep Trypsin/P and record why in the manifest. Either way, document the reconcile adjudication.

findings.message: The defining sample-processing step, anti-succinyllysine antibody enrichment of peptides, is not encoded.
findings.evidence: PRIDE sample protocol: 'succinylated (or acetylated) peptides were enriched using polyclonal antibody beads (immunechem)'. ms-proteomics/sample-metadata templates offer optional characteristics[enrichment process] (EFO:0009090 children).
findings.correction: Optionally add characteristics[enrichment process] with the most specific valid EFO/PRIDE term for antibody-based PTM-peptide enrichment, or a documented 'not available' if none fits.
